newsitem.title: USA: Don't postpone EMU - German opposition politician.
newsitem.headline: Don't postpone EMU - German opposition politician.

text.p: A senior German opposition party politician opposed postponement of the start of European monetary union and suggested that the fiscal criteria for entry could be interpreted flexibly.
"I am against such postponement," Ingrid Matthaus-Maier, spokesperson for financial policy for the Social Democrats (SPD), told the Friedrich Ebert Foundation.

Gerhard Schroeder, a leading member of the Social Democrats, triggered widespread criticism from the government last month when he said that the new European currency would not be as strong as the German mark.
Matthaus-Maier said that Schroeder backed EMU but also seemed to be in favor of postponing its start-up date.
"I'm not very happy about what he's been saying," Matthaus-Maier said. She said that the Social Democrats were in favor of EMU and were a "European-directed" party.
Matthaus-Maier welcomed the budget discipline imposed by the Maastricht Treaty in setting out targets for the reduction of government debt and budget deficits for the launch of EMU.
But she added that the treaty itself allows for some flexibility in interpreting those targets.
She also voiced broad satisfaction with the level of the mark against the dollar, saying the U.S. currency had been undervalued but was now "normal."
